title: Accounting Standard 15 Employee Benefits
outcomes: Classify employee benefits into the four AS 15 categories.
Account for short-term benefits including paid absences and bonus.
Distinguish defined contribution and defined benefit plans and measure defined benefit cost and liability.
Account for other long-term and termination benefits.

meta.exam_tip: For defined benefit questions, prepare separate movements for the obligation and plan assets, then reconcile the net liability.

concepts.title: Scope and the four categories of employee benefits
body: Employee benefits are all forms of consideration an enterprise gives in exchange for service rendered by employees, whether under formal plans, laws, industry arrangements or informal practices that create an obligation.

AS 15 has four categories: short-term benefits (due wholly within twelve months after the period in which service is rendered); post-employment benefits (gratuity, pension, provident fund, post-retirement medical care); other long-term benefits (long-service leave, deferred bonus, long-term disability benefits); and termination benefits (payable on ending employment, such as VRS).
The standard covers employers, not the plans themselves, and does not deal with share-based payments.
concepts.analogy: Every rupee promised for staff service fits one of four boxes, each with its own rule.
concepts.work: Monthly salary is short-term; gratuity is post-employment; a VRS payout is a termination benefit.

concepts.title: Short-term benefits, paid absences and bonus
body: Short-term benefits are recognised as an expense (unless capitalised under another standard) at the undiscounted amount expected to be paid for service rendered in the period, with any unpaid amount as a liability.

Paid absences are accumulating (unused leave can be carried forward) or non-accumulating (lapses). Accumulating absences are recognised as employees render service that increases their entitlement, measured at the extra amount expected to be paid because of the unused entitlement — whether vesting (cash on leaving) or non-vesting. Non-accumulating absences are recognised only when the absence occurs.

Profit-sharing and bonus are recognised when the enterprise has a present obligation (legal or from past practice) and can reliably estimate it. Informal practices can create such an obligation when the enterprise has no realistic alternative but to pay.
concepts.analogy: Pay what is due for this year's work this year, including leave earned but not yet taken.
concepts.work: A customary Diwali bonus paid every year without fail is provided for even without a written contract.

concepts.title: Defined contribution and defined benefit plans
body: Defined contribution plans: the enterprise pays fixed contributions into a fund and has no obligation to pay more if the fund falls short. Actuarial and investment risk fall on the employee. The expense is the contribution payable for the period; amounts due beyond twelve months are discounted.
Defined benefit plans: the enterprise promises a level of benefits, so actuarial and investment risk fall on it. Gratuity and pension promising a formula benefit are typical.
Multi-employer and state plans are classified by their terms; insured benefits are treated as defined contribution if the employer has no further obligation.
concepts.analogy: In a contribution plan you promise a payment in; in a benefit plan you promise a payment out.
concepts.work: Employer's 12% PF contribution to the government fund is a defined contribution; gratuity of 15 days' salary per year is defined benefit.

concepts.title: Measuring defined benefit cost and liability
body: The obligation is measured using the projected unit credit method — each period of service gives rise to an extra unit of benefit — with unbiased and mutually compatible actuarial assumptions about mortality, staff turnover, salary growth and so on.
The discount rate comes from current government bond yields (as at the balance sheet date) for a period matching when the benefits will be paid.
The balance sheet shows the present value of the obligation less the fair value of plan assets (adjusted for unrecognised past service cost); any net asset is limited.

The expense comprises current service cost, interest cost, expected return on plan assets, actuarial gains and losses (recognised immediately in profit and loss), past service cost (immediately if vested, otherwise straight-line until vesting) and the effect of curtailments or settlements.
concepts.analogy: Value the promise with actuarial tools, net off the fund, and show the gap.
concepts.work: A rise in bond yields lowers the obligation and produces an actuarial gain in profit and loss.

concepts.title: Other long-term and termination benefits
body: Other long-term employee benefits are measured like defined benefit obligations, but actuarial gains and losses and past service cost are all recognised immediately in profit and loss.

Termination benefits are recognised as a liability and expense only when the enterprise has a present obligation from a past event, an outflow is probable and a reliable estimate can be made. Amounts due beyond twelve months are discounted. For voluntary schemes, measurement is based on the number of employees expected to accept.
Where the number accepting is uncertain, a contingent liability may exist and is disclosed.
concepts.analogy: Long-term and exit benefits are provided when they are real obligations, without smoothing.
concepts.work: A VRS offered in March with 60 expected acceptances is provided for on that basis at year end.

illustrations.title: Unused leave at the year end
illustrations.q: Pankaj Ltd. lets 100 employees carry forward unused leave for one year (non-vesting). At 31 March each has 5 unused days; experience shows 80% of carried-forward days are actually taken. Average daily pay is ₹2,000. What liability is recognised?

solution.text: The leave is accumulating, so the obligation arises as service is rendered — even though it is non-vesting. The expected usage is what is measured. Non-accumulating leave would be expensed only when taken.

checks.label: Leave days expected to be used from carried-forward balance

illustrations.title: A gratuity plan for the year
illustrations.q: For Anand Ltd.'s funded gratuity plan: opening obligation ₹50,00,000; opening plan assets ₹40,00,000; current service cost ₹6,00,000; discount rate 8%; expected return on assets 9%; contributions paid ₹7,00,000; benefits paid ₹3,00,000; actuarial loss on the obligation ₹1,40,000 (actual return equals expected). Compute the expense and the closing net liability.

solution.text: Check: opening net liability ₹10,00,000 + expense ₹7,80,000 − contributions ₹7,00,000 = ₹10,80,000.

jobs.title: Year-end employee benefit provisions
jobs.situation: You receive an actuary's report for gratuity and leave encashment and HR data on bonus and VRS.
steps: Classify each benefit into the four categories.
Provide for accumulating leave and customary bonus.
Check VRS for a present obligation.

mcqs.q: Short-term employee benefits are measured at:
options: The undiscounted amount expected to be paid
mcqs.explain: Because they fall due within twelve months after the period of service, short-term benefits are recognised at the undiscounted amount the enterprise expects to pay in exchange for that service. In practice: no actuary is needed.
mcqs.topic: Short-term benefits, paid absences and bonus

mcqs.explain: Leave that lapses if not used creates no obligation as service is rendered; the cost is recognised only when the absence actually occurs. Accumulating leave is recognised as service is rendered. In practice: sick leave is often non-accumulating.
mcqs.topic: Short-term benefits, paid absences and bonus

mcqs.q: In a defined contribution plan, investment risk falls on:
mcqs.explain: The employer's obligation is limited to the contributions it agrees to pay, so actuarial and investment risks are borne by employees through the benefits they finally receive. In practice: expense the contribution payable.
mcqs.topic: Defined contribution and defined benefit plans

mcqs.q: The method used to measure a defined benefit obligation is:
mcqs.explain: AS 15 requires the projected unit credit method, which treats each period of service as earning an extra unit of benefit and measures each unit separately to build up the final obligation. In practice: actuaries apply it.
mcqs.topic: Measuring defined benefit cost and liability

mcqs.q: The discount rate for post-employment obligations is based on:
options: Market yields on government bonds at the balance sheet date
mcqs.explain: AS 15 ties the discount rate to year-end government bond yields whose maturity matches the expected payment dates. In practice: longer obligations use longer bond yields.
mcqs.topic: Measuring defined benefit cost and liability

mcqs.q: Under AS 15, actuarial gains and losses on defined benefit plans are recognised:
options: Immediately in the statement of profit and loss
mcqs.explain: AS 15 requires actuarial gains and losses to be recognised immediately in profit and loss, which keeps the balance sheet at the full net obligation. In practice: they can make profits volatile.
mcqs.topic: Measuring defined benefit cost and liability

mcqs.q: Current service cost ₹4 lakh; interest cost ₹3 lakh; expected return on assets ₹2.5 lakh; actuarial gain ₹0.5 lakh. Expense:
mcqs.explain: Expense = 4 + 3 − 2.5 − 0.5 = ₹4 lakh: service and interest add cost, while expected return and the actuarial gain reduce it. In practice: list components separately in the note.
mcqs.topic: Measuring defined benefit cost and liability

mcqs.q: Past service cost that has already vested is:
options: Spread over the remaining service life
mcqs.explain: Vested past service cost is recognised immediately; non-vested past service cost is recognised on a straight-line basis over the average period until the benefits become vested. In practice: plan amendments trigger this.
mcqs.topic: Measuring defined benefit cost and liability

mcqs.q: Actuarial gains and losses on other long-term benefits such as long-service leave are:
options: Recognised immediately in profit and loss
mcqs.explain: Other long-term benefits are measured like defined benefit obligations but with a simpler rule: actuarial gains and losses and past service cost are all recognised immediately in profit and loss. In practice: actuarial valuation is still needed.

mcqs.q: Termination benefits under a voluntary scheme are measured based on:
options: The number of employees expected to accept the offer
mcqs.explain: Where an offer encourages voluntary separation, AS 15 bases the measurement on how many staff are likely to take up the offer. Uncertainty about numbers may also require a contingent liability disclosure. In practice: use HR estimates.

questions.q: Pankaj Ltd. lets 100 employees carry forward unused leave for one year (non-vesting). At 31 March each has 5 unused days; experience shows 80% of carried-forward days are actually taken. Average daily pay is ₹2,000. What liability is recognised?

model.text: The leave is accumulating, so the obligation arises as service is rendered — even though it is non-vesting. The expected usage is what is measured. Non-accumulating leave would be expensed only when taken.

scheme.pt: Accumulating leave recognised as service is rendered

checks.label: Leave days expected to be used from carried-forward balance

questions.q: For Anand Ltd.'s funded gratuity plan: opening obligation ₹50,00,000; opening plan assets ₹40,00,000; current service cost ₹6,00,000; discount rate 8%; expected return on assets 9%; contributions paid ₹7,00,000; benefits paid ₹3,00,000; actuarial loss on the obligation ₹1,40,000 (actual return equals expected). Compute the expense and the closing net liability.

model.text: Check: opening net liability ₹10,00,000 + expense ₹7,80,000 − contributions ₹7,00,000 = ₹10,80,000.

summary: Four categories: short-term, post-employment, other long-term, termination.
Short-term: undiscounted; accumulating leave as service is rendered.
Bonus when a present obligation exists (including practice).
DC: expense contribution; DB: projected unit credit, gov bond discount rate.
DB expense: service + interest − expected return ± actuarial + past service ± curtailment.
Long-term: immediate recognition; termination: when obligation exists.
remember: Actuarial gains/losses go to profit and loss immediately.
traps: Non-vesting accumulating leave still creates a liability.

viva.q: Name the four categories of employee benefits.
viva.model: Short-term benefits, post-employment benefits, other long-term benefits and termination benefits.

viva.q: Distinguish defined contribution from defined benefit plans.
viva.model: In a defined contribution plan the employer pays fixed contributions and bears no further risk; in a defined benefit plan the employer promises the benefit and bears actuarial and investment risk.

points.pt: Risk on employer for benefit plans

viva.q: When is a customary bonus provided for?
viva.model: When the enterprise has a present obligation, legal or arising from past practice with no realistic alternative but to pay, and the amount can be reliably estimated.

viva.q: What are the components of defined benefit expense?
viva.model: Current service cost, interest cost, expected return on plan assets, actuarial gains and losses, past service cost and effects of curtailments or settlements.

viva.q: How is accumulating paid absence measured?
viva.model: At the additional amount the enterprise expects to pay because of the unused entitlement that has built up at the balance sheet date.

cases.title: Unnati Steel Ltd.
cases.case: Unnati Steel Ltd. contributes 12% of basic pay to the government provident fund (₹48 lakh for the year, ₹4 lakh unpaid at year end). It runs a gratuity plan valued by an actuary, and in March announced a VRS; 40 employees are expected to accept at ₹5 lakh each.

mcqs.q: The provident fund expense for the year is:
options: ₹48 lakh, with ₹4 lakh shown as a liability
mcqs.explain: A defined contribution plan is expensed at the contribution payable for the period, ₹48 lakh, and the unpaid ₹4 lakh is a liability. No actuarial valuation is needed. In practice: pay dues on time.
mcqs.topic: Defined contribution and defined benefit plans

mcqs.explain: Gratuity promises a benefit based on salary and years of service, so the employer bears actuarial and investment risk: it is a defined benefit plan. In practice: use the projected unit credit method.
mcqs.topic: Defined contribution and defined benefit plans

mcqs.q: Provision for the VRS at year end:
mcqs.explain: With a present obligation from the announced scheme, termination benefits are measured on the number expected to accept: 40 × ₹5 lakh = ₹2 crore. In practice: discount if payable beyond twelve months.
